THE KITCHEN FACTORY

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a kitchen renovator that royally rips of clients leaving them with half finished kitchens and broke!

Unique Selling Point:
LEKKER CONSUMER STORY - GREAT BADDIE WITH A TRACK RECORD AND A PENCHANT FOR THREATENING HIS CLIENTS!

Summary:
Home renovations are often the realisation of a long term dream for many home owners - but customers of Brian Gomes and his Kitchen Factory will tell you their dream turned into a disaster - leaving them out of pocket with unfinised kitchens in their homes.

We go undercover and expose this kitchen crook!

Further information:
Brian Gomes is behind The Kitchen Factory and now his newest venture Custom Kitchens Factory. He's been running a racket for years ripping off a rainbow nation of customers...I have 9 case studies dating back to 2012 - all telling the same sorry tales about bad workmanship and unfinished kitchens - customers have paid between 50 - 80 000 Rand for kitchens and then still have to cough up more money to finish the job and buy materials ranging from hinges to door handles to counter tops. The little work The Kitchen Factory does could take weeks to materialise and still not be completed. But the best part about this baddie is that he comes with attitude - Mr. Gomes takes to threatening customers who complain - he's so brazen, he sends these threats via emails and psychically assaulted the one case study!

The Modus Operandi is simple:
He impresses clients with speedy quotes and designs. Promises delivery within days - he has his own factory that manufactures cupboards - demands 50% up front,takes weeks to do a bit of work, then demands the next 40% and then downs tools. The Kitchen Factory workers don't return and customers have to beg and plead for them to finish the job. In the end after threats and drama - Brian Gomes tells the client to keep the last 10% and finish the job with that money - BUT the outstanding work will cost a lot more than the balance - often the more expensive materials like counter tops, basins and taps have not been delivered. He also promises one thing and delivers another.


I have found 9 case studies - we'll feature three on camera. There have been positive reports on consumer sites - will work it in.

CASE STUDY 1 - Nonthlanthla Ranape
Paid R80 000 and spent an additional R50 000 to finish The Kitchen Factory's mess. (she has pictures of the state things were left in and access to the house - she has since sold it)
I paid Kitchen Factory to do my Kitchen, BIC for en-suite, and vanity, I was rushed to pay the 50% deposit in December 2012; I have the proof of payment with the promise that the work will start on the 16 January 2013. I had to call and send emails for Kitchen Factory to confirm the start date; I was told to pay the 30% of the remaining 50% for them to release the goods; I paid the 30%, they started working last week of January 2013. The owner Brian Gomes promised that they will finish all the work in 3-4 weeks. Most of the time I have to call to check when are they coming to finish working I will be promised and when they come they would be there for half a day and go. I the resorted to writing e-mails because I need all my conversations documented.
There are so many things that are wrong and not according to the agreed specification, when I enquire I am victimized, (emails from Mr Gomes are available). The outstanding amount owed to The Kitchen Factory is /-R3800.00. The work cost an additional 50 000.00 to finish.

CASE STUDY 2 - Shaun van den Brught
Paid over R46 000 and still needs to spend another R32 000 to finish his kitchen (it's half finished at the moment)
Gomes Homes Pty Ltd T/A The Kitchen Factory contractually undertook to complete my kitchen in December 2015 and to date has failed to supply stone counter tops, sinks, handles and glass doors. The total costs of materials that were not supplied exceed R32,000, this excludes the costs of replacing the low quality workmanship and cutting errors made by the company.

CASE STUDY 3 - Lawrence de Rozario (Emmigrated to SA from the UK 4 years ago - is frustrated with the terrible quality workmanship)
He spent R60 000 for a kitchen that is of poor quality and unfixable - he's gotten quotes to do repairs but has been told the only way to fix it, is to rip it out and start over again. (he says the shoddy workmanship is evident)
BACKGROUND TO HIS STORY
The main reason for using the Kitchen Factory was because they said they could have the units built in 3 days. I paid the 50% deposit & I was told that another 40% would be payable to release my order. Almost 2 weeks later the owner Brian & the factory manager Kevin called & emailed early in the morning chasing the 40%. After paying the 40% I was told that they actually hadn’t finished all the units & they were still waiting for materials. In total it took 6-7 weeks for them to deliver the kitchen as things came in drips & drabs.
A large proportion of the units were completely wrong - e.g. wrong sizes - or damaged. Technically all were wrong as I ordered white units with white trim but I received units that were a mixture of white & brown with brown trim.

The quality of the units is extremely poor. The majority of the doors, drawers, units & side panels are chipped because I have found out that they used the wrong type of saw blade. There are also many scratches & one of the units came with gouges in the exposed sides. None of the 15 drawers are level, they point downwards, & it’s extremely hard to open them because the runners. The drawers in the drawer units rub against each other & where there are units with a door & a drawer, the drawers rub on the doors.

Shelves are not level & some wobble because they’re too narrow or because the holes for the shelf supports have been incorrectly drilled. The shelf for the microwave is actually bowing as it was made with no supports. The frosted glass doors are patchy & have been damaged by the fitter.

They have supplied inferior quality items to what I ordered. I ordered soft closing hinges & runners. I have been informed by another kitchen company they have used the wrong type of hinges were used as in they are not meant for kitchen units. The runners are not soft closing but standard ball bearing runners. The majority of the drawers do not open properly & the runners are either stiff or broken. Kevin said grit has got in them when they fitted them. The ball bearing came out of one of the runners when my wife opened the drawer for the first time & some of the other the runners are also broken. I ordered aluminium kick plates but I received plastic kickplates with a very thin foil on the front. Some of the items I paid for were not delivered such as side panels which were no cheap.



HOW TO DO IT
We set up a sting - get The Kitchen Factory to come out and quote to do a kitchen - that way we get their sales pitch on camera and will hopefully get some info on the company on camera.

CONFRONT AT THEIR OFFICES / FACTORY

There is also another company using the same name in Brakpan - they have picked up a lot of flack from Brian Gomes dodgy dealings.

We'll include a representative from the Kitchen Specialist Association for guidelines and professional opinions on the workmanship.

Press Release:


Kitchen Crooks
An expensive investment and the realisation of a dream, but many home owners don’t realise that the wrong contractor could turn their dream
kitchen into a nightmare. Carte Blanche exposes a renovator who has left several clients out of pocket and stuck with half-finished kitchens.

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Thousands of South African homes are transformed with home renovations worth millions of Rands every year, with kitchens being the most expensive part of the make over.

LINK: It’s an investment – the realisation of a long-term dream, but what many people don’t realise is that you get what you pay for – and this could turn into a nightmare.

VO: Stephanie Forbes is from The Kitchen Specialists Association or KSA.

STEPHANIE: Anyone who knows the difference between a flat head and phillips screw driver can start a kitchen company – we don’t have qualifications or regulation.

VO: She says kitchen companies that reel in deals with impressive and exaggerated sales pitches are a dime a dozen.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER KITCHEN FACTORY SALES PERSON: our factory is geared for call it 500 a month – we do between 8 and 16 installations a day.

VO: These three homeowners were impressed by their initial dealings with The Kitchen Factory in the south of Johannesburg and chose them to do the job.

NONHLANHLA: They were the lowest and they had the nice design.
LAWRENCE: They said they could build the kitchen in three days.
SHAUN: they were manufacturer suppliers and not just retailers.

VO: But the reality is, because the industry is unregulated - many companies over promise and often under deliver - if at all.

The KSA is a voluntary organisation – its members choose to be held accountable by a panel of their peers. But when you’re dealing with a non-member, consumers have very little recourse.

STEPHANIE: other than going to the consumer protector – there’s not much else they go other than coming to the media. - if you are not a member we don’t have any legal jurisdiction to make a call or hold you accountable for your workmanship.

VO: Brian Gomes is the man behind The Kitchen Factory. They have been in the business for decades, but are not registered with the KSA.

DEVI – Why not registed with KSa
BRIAN – never registered – // I never had it in all the years – three unhappy clients // // But I mean I can put you onto a thousand happy clients,

LINK LAWRENCE HOUSE: This is not too shabby – modern and expensive looking… at R70 000 just for the cupboards – you’d think this quality, but there’s something I want to show you … looks can be deceiving….

VO: Lawrence De Rozario is not one of the many happy clients.

He dealt with The Kitchen Factory in July 2016.
They quoted close to R71 000 [R70913,70] for just the cupboards.

He says the workmanship was simply not up to scratch.

LAWRENCE: The first time we opened it – ball bearings came out – all over the floor. ST3 M8
DEVI: How many doors have fallen off?
LAWRENCE: Only two so far – but there are a few that can fall down soon //ST3 M3

STEPHANIE: // a lot of what a good kitchen is you cant see – it’s the quality of the board that is used for the carcassing, the hinges and runners – those are the things that give you the 5, 10 year longevity of your kitchen // NOT GONNA LAST 5 YEARS.

BRIAN: I have kitchens that have been standing for 20 years

VO: Stephanie pointed out that - this installation itself is poor and that it’s only a matter of time before the oven comes crashing down.

STEPHANIE: basically all they’ve got is the chip board carcasses – you can see that hinges haven’t been installed properly.

VO: Lucien Pierce is a consumer protection law expert, he says consumers are not without rights.

LUCIEN: you’re entitled to expect a reasonable product // standard // you didn’t get what you ordered…

VO: Shaun van der Burght dealt with the Kitchen Factory between 2015 and 2016.

He was quoted just over R66 000 – [R66 169,57] for the kitchen including tops & materials.

With issues around installation and quality – the relationship broke down between Shaun and The Kitchen Factory after heated arguments.

BRIAN: that shaun guy – at the end of the day – came to a point – we can’t please you.

VO: At this stage, Shaun had already paid over 90% of the total. (R59552,69) – but had yet to receive most of the materials.

SHAUN: But even if the fact that I am fussy is not a reason // to not supply the materials of which you paid for – which exceeds 40% of the value of what you’ve already committed – that’s theft. INT6 M14

DEVI: // He says you still have got his stuff. M29
BRIAN: no he came here and loaded a bakkie load of stuff… with police…

VO: But Brian was of the opinion that Shaun was the thief.

DEVI: You’re saying he’s got everything you owe him and more! M30
BRIAN: Yah, he’s got other clients stuff,

VO: But Shaun and Juan, the contractor that finished the cupboard installation, have a different version.

JUAN: What happened is we didn’t load it ourselves. The workers at the factory – they loaded it onto the bakkie. And everything actually fitted the kitchen as it should have.

VO: While he eventually got his cupboards, Shaun says he never received the worktops, double sink, prepbowl, dustbin and door handles . The worktops alone cost over R19 000 [R19 446,12].

DEVI: Did you deliver tops?
BRIAN: no
DEVI: Was tops part of the deal?
BRIAN: YES
DEVI: So where are the tops?
BRIAN: everything fell apart at the point M35

VO: BUT WHAT RECOURSE DOES SHAUN HAVE?

LUCIEN: Because he’s not a member of any particular industry association - the only route they have is got to the consumer commission.

VO: But even then the company in question will only be issued a fine.

LUCIEN: If it’s cost them a lot more they go against him in the civil courts.

VO: After numerous attempts to get a refund, Shaun took the matter to the Small Claims Court, the judgement was in his favour. Brian has not paid back the money and plans to challenge the ruling.

He insists these cases are only one or two % of his clientele base and that he has many happy clients. To be fair we called one of Brian’s bigger clients – property developer Tony Phinero – Brian has done work for him since 2013.

TONY – Dozens of them for me.
DEVI – any comebacks
TONY– I very much not serious - haven’t had really a problem, no

VO: Brian sent us a list of many more happy developers and private clients – we called several of them, who confirmed this.

UPSOUND – KEVIN PALMER: It was great, it was fantastic. It was the best aspect of renovation in terms of service. //

VO: But it seems that a number of clients don’t share this view.

Stephanie says - complaints are not uncommon in the kitchen industry.

DEVI: Do you get lots of complaints
STEPHANIE: it’s growing since we’ve seen the advent of the CPA we’ve seen a massive increase.
DEVI: What kinds of complaints
STEPHANIE: people looking to cut corners cost wise, sometimes it’s just people being unreasonable be it the client or the kitchen company.

VO: Brian blamed Lawrence for problems with the installation of the kitchen, saying he designed his own kitchen based on UK expectations, and if anything was incorrect – it was because of Lawrence’s own measurements.

BRIAN: We made it according to his dimension M53//we made it according to his dimensions. // M49

VO: However, an email from Brian to Lawrence seems to contradict this – he stated that they will come measure up. Lawrence confirmed they did, but without the plans.

NONHLANHLA: Mr. Gomes is not a very honourable man // he saw me as woman he could take advantage of.

VO: Nonthlanhla Ranape dealt with The Kitchen Factory end 2012 / 2013 – she has subsequently sold that house. The original quote was for R161000 – and included a new kitchen, built in cupboards and a bathroom vanity. [R161330].

She paid a 50% deposit in December with the undertaking the job would start in the new year.

NONHLANHLA: I was promised two weeks and it took more than 4 weeks to complete. INT6 M4 // You can imagine my frustration now, I have already paid him and now I am worried about my money. INT1 M25 // its sitting with him // now I have to beg him. INT1 M26

VO: Just like Lawrence & Shaun, Nonhlanhla was equally unhappy with her kitchen fitment.

NONHLANHLA: // the eye level is hanging out, the pantry door is dragging,– //INT2 M20// the broken tiles, the cabinet had pigeon holes for the towels – they were not symmetric, they were not proper. INT3 M10

DEVI – installation problems
BRIAN – of course – becomes a snag and then we fix and done – we can fix until it’s done. M87

VO: But that didn’t happen with these three clients – they say Brian avoided contact when they started getting upset about delays and shoddy workmanship.

LAWRENCE: He basically said to me that they aren’t going to do anymore work – and that I should keep the 10% and get someone else to finish the job.

VO: Stephanie says this is a common occurrence in the industry with unregistered operators.

STEPHANIE: they have made their money – they can walk away scot-free- they haven’t made a loss on the job.

VO: But these clients will have to cough up a lot more than the outstanding 10% to fix and finish the work.

Lawrence is in for another R20 000 plus.

While Brian credited Nonhlanhla for some materials - she paid up in full – but had to get a carpenter and a plumber to finish – forking out an additional R12000 in labour.

SHAUN has spent another R27 000 and has ten more to go – he says he has learnt his lesson.

SHAUN: Find a reputable company that belongs perhaps to the Kitchen Specialist Association and pay that extra bit – don’t hesitate in terms of thinking I am going to save a few thousand rand here and there







PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 10 seconds
VO: Kitchen renovation dreams can turn into a nightmares if not done by registered operators.

STEPHANIE: // Anyone who knows the difference between a flat head and phillips screw driver can start a kitchen company // INT1 M3

PROMO 2
VO: When it comes to kitchen makeovers - opting for the cheapest quote could cost you in the long run.

STEPHANIE: it’s the quality of the board that is used for the carcassing, the hinges and runners – those are the things that give you the 5, 10 year longevity of your kitchen

PROMO 3
VO: When your kitchen renovation turns into a nightmare - you may be left in jam with very little recourse if the company is not registered the KSA.

STEPHANIE: if you are not a member we don’t have any legal jurisdiction to make a call or hold you accountable for your workmanship.

DEVI – Why not registed with KSa BRIAN – never registered – // I never had it in all the years – three unhappy clients // // But I mean I can put you onto a thousand happy clients, LINK LAWRENCE HOUSE: This is not too shabby – modern and expensive looking… at R70 000 just for the cupboards – you’d think this quality, but there’s something I want to show you … looks can be deceiving…. VO: Lawrence De Rozario is not one of the many happy clients. He dealt with The Kitchen Factory in July 2016. They quoted close to R71 000 [R70913,70] for just the cupboards. He says the workmanship was simply not up to scratch. LAWRENCE: The first time we opened it – ball bearings came out – all over the floor. ST3 M8 DEVI: How many doors have fallen off? LAWRENCE: Only two so far – but there are a few that can fall down soon //ST3 M3 STEPHANIE: // a lot of what a good kitchen is you cant see – it’s the quality of the board that is used for the carcassing, the hinges and runners – those are the things that give you the 5, 10 year longevity of your kitchen // NOT GONNA LAST 5 YEARS. BRIAN: I have kitchens that have been standing for 20 years VO: Stephanie pointed out that - this installation itself is poor and that it’s only a matter of time before the oven comes crashing down. STEPHANIE: basically all they’ve got is the chip board carcasses – you can see that hinges haven’t been installed properly. VO: Lucien Pierce is a consumer protection law expert, he says consumers are not without rights. LUCIEN: you’re entitled to expect a reasonable product // standard // you didn’t get what you ordered… VO: Shaun van der Burght dealt with the Kitchen Factory between 2015 and 2016. He was quoted just over R66 000 – [R66 169,57] for the kitchen including tops & materials. With issues around installation and quality – the relationship broke down between Shaun and The Kitchen Factory after heated arguments. BRIAN: that shaun guy – at the end of the day – came to a point – we can’t please you. VO: At this stage, Shaun had already paid over 90% of the total. (R59552,69) – but had yet to receive most of the materials. SHAUN: But even if the fact that I am fussy is not a reason // to not supply the materials of which you paid for – which exceeds 40% of the value of what you’ve already committed – that’s theft. INT6 M14 DEVI: // He says you still have got his stuff. M29 BRIAN: no he came here and loaded a bakkie load of stuff… with police… VO: But Brian was of the opinion that Shaun was the thief. DEVI: You’re saying he’s got everything you owe him and more! M30 BRIAN: Yah, he’s got other clients stuff, VO: But Shaun and Juan, the contractor that finished the cupboard installation, have a different version. JUAN: What happened is we didn’t load it ourselves. The workers at the factory – they loaded it onto the bakkie. And everything actually fitted the kitchen as it should have. VO: While he eventually got his cupboards, Shaun says he never received the worktops, double sink, prepbowl, dustbin and door handles . The worktops alone cost over R19 000 [R19 446,12]. DEVI: Did you deliver tops? BRIAN: no DEVI: Was tops part of the deal? BRIAN: YES DEVI: So where are the tops? BRIAN: everything fell apart at the point M35 VO: BUT WHAT RECOURSE DOES SHAUN HAVE? LUCIEN: Because he’s not a member of any particular industry association - the only route they have is got to the consumer commission. VO: But even then the company in question will only be issued a fine. LUCIEN: If it’s cost them a lot more they go against him in the civil courts. VO: After numerous attempts to get a refund, Shaun took the matter to the Small Claims Court, the judgement was in his favour. Brian has not paid back the money and plans to challenge the ruling. He insists these cases are only one or two % of his clientele base and that he has many happy clients. To be fair we called one of Brian’s bigger clients – property developer Tony Phinero – Brian has done work for him since 2013. TONY – Dozens of them for me. DEVI – any comebacks TONY– I very much not serious - haven’t had really a problem, no VO: Brian sent us a list of many more happy developers and private clients – we called several of them, who confirmed this. UPSOUND – KEVIN PALMER: It was great, it was fantastic. It was the best aspect of renovation in terms of service. // VO: But it seems that a number of clients don’t share this view. Stephanie says - complaints are not uncommon in the kitchen industry. DEVI: Do you get lots of complaints STEPHANIE: it’s growing since we’ve seen the advent of the CPA we’ve seen a massive increase. DEVI: What kinds of complaints STEPHANIE: people looking to cut corners cost wise, sometimes it’s just people being unreasonable be it the client or the kitchen company. VO: Brian blamed Lawrence for problems with the installation of the kitchen, saying he designed his own kitchen based on UK expectations, and if anything was incorrect – it was because of Lawrence’s own measurements. BRIAN: We made it according to his dimension M53//we made it according to his dimensions. // M49 VO: However, an email from Brian to Lawrence seems to contradict this – he stated that they will come measure up. Lawrence confirmed they did, but without the plans. NONHLANHLA: Mr. Gomes is not a very honourable man // he saw me as woman he could take advantage of. VO: Nonthlanhla Ranape dealt with The Kitchen Factory end 2012 / 2013 – she has subsequently sold that house. The original quote was for R161000 – and included a new kitchen, built in cupboards and a bathroom vanity. [R161330]. She paid a 50% deposit in December with the undertaking the job would start in the new year. NONHLANHLA: I was promised two weeks and it took more than 4 weeks to complete. INT6 M4 // You can imagine my frustration now, I have already paid him and now I am worried about my money. INT1 M25 // its sitting with him // now I have to beg him. INT1 M26 VO: Just like Lawrence & Shaun, Nonhlanhla was equally unhappy with her kitchen fitment. NONHLANHLA: // the eye level is hanging out, the pantry door is dragging,– //INT2 M20// the broken tiles, the cabinet had pigeon holes for the towels – they were not symmetric, they were not proper. INT3 M10 DEVI – installation problems BRIAN – of course – becomes a snag and then we fix and done – we can fix until it’s done. M87 VO: But that didn’t happen with these three clients – they say Brian avoided contact when they started getting upset about delays and shoddy workmanship. LAWRENCE: He basically said to me that they aren’t going to do anymore work – and that I should keep the 10% and get someone else to finish the job. VO: Stephanie says this is a common occurrence in the industry with unregistered operators. STEPHANIE: they have made their money – they can walk away scot-free- they haven’t made a loss on the job. VO: But these clients will have to cough up a lot more than the outstanding 10% to fix and finish the work. Lawrence is in for another R20 000 plus. While Brian credited Nonhlanhla for some materials - she paid up in full – but had to get a carpenter and a plumber to finish – forking out an additional R12000 in labour. SHAUN has spent another R27 000 and has ten more to go – he says he has learnt his lesson. SHAUN: Find a reputable company that belongs perhaps to the Kitchen Specialist Association and pay that extra bit – don’t hesitate in terms of thinking I am going to save a few thousand rand here and there PROMOS PROMO 1 – 10 seconds VO: Kitchen renovation dreams can turn into a nightmares if not done by registered operators. STEPHANIE: // Anyone who knows the difference between a flat head and phillips screw driver can start a kitchen company // INT1 M3 PROMO 2 VO: When it comes to kitchen makeovers - opting for the cheapest quote could cost you in the long run. STEPHANIE: it’s the quality of the board that is used for the carcassing, the hinges and runners – those are the things that give you the 5, 10 year longevity of your kitchen PROMO 3 VO: When your kitchen renovation turns into a nightmare - you may be left in jam with very little recourse if the company is not registered the KSA. STEPHANIE: if you are not a member we don’t have any legal jurisdiction to make a call or hold you accountable for your workmanship. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose a kitchen renovator that royally rips of clients leaving them with half finished kitchens and broke!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: LEKKER CONSUMER STORY - GREAT BADDIE WITH A TRACK RECORD AND A PENCHANT FOR THREATENING HIS CLIENTS!
metadata.Summary: Home renovations are often the realisation of a long term dream for many home owners - but customers of Brian Gomes and his Kitchen Factory will tell you their dream turned into a disaster - leaving them out of pocket with unfinised kitchens in their homes. We go undercover and expose this kitchen crook!
metadata.Further information: Brian Gomes is behind The Kitchen Factory and now his newest venture Custom Kitchens Factory. He's been running a racket for years ripping off a rainbow nation of customers...I have 9 case studies dating back to 2012 - all telling the same sorry tales about bad workmanship and unfinished kitchens - customers have paid between 50 - 80 000 Rand for kitchens and then still have to cough up more money to finish the job and buy materials ranging from hinges to door handles to counter tops. The little work The Kitchen Factory does could take weeks to materialise and still not be completed. But the best part about this baddie is that he comes with attitude - Mr. Gomes takes to threatening customers who complain - he's so brazen, he sends these threats via emails and psychically assaulted the one case study! The Modus Operandi is simple: He impresses clients with speedy quotes and designs. Promises delivery within days - he has his own factory that manufactures cupboards - demands 50% up front,takes weeks to do a bit of work, then demands the next 40% and then downs tools. The Kitchen Factory workers don't return and customers have to beg and plead for them to finish the job. In the end after threats and drama - Brian Gomes tells the client to keep the last 10% and finish the job with that money - BUT the outstanding work will cost a lot more than the balance - often the more expensive materials like counter tops, basins and taps have not been delivered. He also promises one thing and delivers another. I have found 9 case studies - we'll feature three on camera. There have been positive reports on consumer sites - will work it in. CASE STUDY 1 - Nonthlanthla Ranape Paid R80 000 and spent an additional R50 000 to finish The Kitchen Factory's mess. (she has pictures of the state things were left in and access to the house - she has since sold it) I paid Kitchen Factory to do my Kitchen, BIC for en-suite, and vanity, I was rushed to pay the 50% deposit in December 2012; I have the proof of payment with the promise that the work will start on the 16 January 2013. I had to call and send emails for Kitchen Factory to confirm the start date; I was told to pay the 30% of the remaining 50% for them to release the goods; I paid the 30%, they started working last week of January 2013. The owner Brian Gomes promised that they will finish all the work in 3-4 weeks. Most of the time I have to call to check when are they coming to finish working I will be promised and when they come they would be there for half a day and go. I the resorted to writing e-mails because I need all my conversations documented. There are so many things that are wrong and not according to the agreed specification, when I enquire I am victimized, (emails from Mr Gomes are available). The outstanding amount owed to The Kitchen Factory is /-R3800.00. The work cost an additional 50 000.00 to finish. CASE STUDY 2 - Shaun van den Brught Paid over R46 000 and still needs to spend another R32 000 to finish his kitchen (it's half finished at the moment) Gomes Homes Pty Ltd T/A The Kitchen Factory contractually undertook to complete my kitchen in December 2015 and to date has failed to supply stone counter tops, sinks, handles and glass doors. The total costs of materials that were not supplied exceed R32,000, this excludes the costs of replacing the low quality workmanship and cutting errors made by the company. CASE STUDY 3 - Lawrence de Rozario (Emmigrated to SA from the UK 4 years ago - is frustrated with the terrible quality workmanship) He spent R60 000 for a kitchen that is of poor quality and unfixable - he's gotten quotes to do repairs but has been told the only way to fix it, is to rip it out and start over again. (he says the shoddy workmanship is evident) BACKGROUND TO HIS STORY The main reason for using the Kitchen Factory was because they said they could have the units built in 3 days. I paid the 50% deposit & I was told that another 40% would be payable to release my order. Almost 2 weeks later the owner Brian & the factory manager Kevin called & emailed early in the morning chasing the 40%. After paying the 40% I was told that they actually hadn’t finished all the units & they were still waiting for materials. In total it took 6-7 weeks for them to deliver the kitchen as things came in drips & drabs. A large proportion of the units were completely wrong - e.g. wrong sizes - or damaged. Technically all were wrong as I ordered white units with white trim but I received units that were a mixture of white & brown with brown trim. The quality of the units is extremely poor. The majority of the doors, drawers, units & side panels are chipped because I have found out that they used the wrong type of saw blade. There are also many scratches & one of the units came with gouges in the exposed sides. None of the 15 drawers are level, they point downwards, & it’s extremely hard to open them because the runners. The drawers in the drawer units rub against each other & where there are units with a door & a drawer, the drawers rub on the doors. Shelves are not level & some wobble because they’re too narrow or because the holes for the shelf supports have been incorrectly drilled. The shelf for the microwave is actually bowing as it was made with no supports. The frosted glass doors are patchy & have been damaged by the fitter. They have supplied inferior quality items to what I ordered. I ordered soft closing hinges & runners. I have been informed by another kitchen company they have used the wrong type of hinges were used as in they are not meant for kitchen units. The runners are not soft closing but standard ball bearing runners. The majority of the drawers do not open properly & the runners are either stiff or broken. Kevin said grit has got in them when they fitted them. The ball bearing came out of one of the runners when my wife opened the drawer for the first time & some of the other the runners are also broken. I ordered aluminium kick plates but I received plastic kickplates with a very thin foil on the front. Some of the items I paid for were not delivered such as side panels which were no cheap. HOW TO DO IT We set up a sting - get The Kitchen Factory to come out and quote to do a kitchen - that way we get their sales pitch on camera and will hopefully get some info on the company on camera. CONFRONT AT THEIR OFFICES / FACTORY There is also another company using the same name in Brakpan - they have picked up a lot of flack from Brian Gomes dodgy dealings. We'll include a representative from the Kitchen Specialist Association for guidelines and professional opinions on the workmanship.
